items.stem:
Read the survey report and answer the questions that follow.

A survey on how students travel to school was carried out in Agra in 2025. 300 students were asked how they usually travel to school. The results were: walking – 25%; cycling – 15%; school bus – 10%; public transport – 8%; private car or two-wheeler – 42%. The organisers said the findings would help them plan better, and they encouraged people to think about how they commute and use their time and resources.

(i) By how many percentage points does "private car or two-wheeler" differ from "public transport"?  (a) 34  (b) 39  (c) 31  (d) 50
(ii) Did more than half of the students choose "private car or two-wheeler"? Give the figure.
(iii) Which of these statements is supported by the survey?  (a) "private car or two-wheeler" was chosen by more students than "walking".  (b) Every response was chosen by the same number of students.  (c) "public transport" was chosen by more students than "private car or two-wheeler".  (d) The survey was carried out in Delhi.
(iv) Suggest one reason why "public transport" may have been chosen by so few students.
(v) Write one suggestion the organisers could make, based on the survey on how students travel to school.
items.answer: (i) (a) 34 (ii) No – 42%, which is less than half. (iii) (a) "private car or two-wheeler" was chosen by more students than "walking". (iv) Any sensible reason linked to the context (cost, habit, lack of access, awareness, time) – 1 mark. (v) Any practical suggestion that follows from the figures – 1 mark.
items.markingKey: (i) (a) 34 (ii) No – 42%, which is less than half. (iii) (a) "private car or two-wheeler" was chosen by more students than "walking". (iv) Any sensible reason linked to the context (cost, habit, lack of access, awareness, time) – 1 mark. (v) Any practical suggestion that follows from the figures – 1 mark. (1 mark each.)
